description: After fz-sc8.183.1-.3 a step of <<c, r :: binary>> still calls the runtime for the bit length (fz_bs_bit_len_ref), for the byte (fz_bs_read_int_ref) and for a view of the rest (fz_bs_read_binary_ref, 1 allocation). Release, 20.6 MB / 32,000 log lines: read + JSON.decode! keeping nothing takes 3.7 s (measured with integer patterns, before .183.2); Elixir 0.12 s. BEAM keeps a match context (base, offset, end) in registers and reuses it across the self-call, so a step is a load, a compare and an add. Goal: field reads are inline loads against a base pointer and bit length resolved once per function, and a self-recursive walk passes the position instead of building the rest. Needs a spike with predictions and a proposal page before building.
title: A binary walk reads bytes inline and passes its position
